'''George Kollias''' ([[Greek language|Greek]]: Γιώργος Κόλλιας; born 9 November 1958 in [[Athens]]) is a Greek biologist, Member of the [[Academy of Athens (modern)|Academy of Athens]] and Professor of Physiology at the Medical School of the [[National and Kapodistrian University of Athens]]. He is renowned for providing the preclinical rationale for the development of [[TNF inhibitor|anti-TNF]] therapies for [[rheumatoid arthritis]].<ref name="pmid1721867">{{cite journal |vauthors=Keffer J, Probert L, Cazlaris H, Georgopoulos S, Kaslaris E, Kioussis D, Kollias G | title = Transgenic mice expressing human tumour necrosis factor: a predictive genetic model of arthritis | journal = The EMBO Journal | volume = 10 | issue = 13 | pages = 4025–31 |date=December 1991 | pmid = 1721867 | pmc = 453150 | doi = 10.1002/j.1460-2075.1991.tb04978.x}}</ref><ref name="pmid26008591">{{cite journal |vauthors=Brenner D, Blaser H, Mak TW | title = Regulation of tumour necrosis factor signalling: live or let die. | journal = Nat Rev Immunol | volume = 15 | issue = 6 | pages = 362–74 | date=May 2015 | pmid = 26008591 | doi=10.1038/nri3834| s2cid = 1550839 | url = https://orbilu.uni.lu/bitstream/10993/58011/1/Brenner%20and%20Blaser%20et%20al_Nature%20Reviews%20Immunol%202015.pdf }}</ref> His research<ref>{{Cite web |title=Overview |url=https://www.fleming.gr/research/ibi/researchers/kollias-lab |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250123080308/https://www.fleming.gr/research/ibi/researchers/kollias-lab |archive-date=2025-01-23 |access-date=2026-01-15 |website=www.fleming.gr has made pioneering discoveries on the pivotal role of fibroblasts in pathophysiology, instigating a new field opening therapeutic opportunities for chronic inflammation and fibrotic of major national infrastructures of scientific and technological excellence in Greece, such as [https://www.infrafrontier.gr/ InfrafrontierGR] and [https://www.precisionmedicine.gr/ pMedGR]. He is Founder and President of [https://www.biomedcode.com/ BIOMEDCODE HELLAS SA], a CRO offering preclinical drug evaluation services. He is also Founder and Director of [https://www.inolysis.com/ INOLYSIS], a company developing novel therapeutics against chronic inflammation and fibrosis.

== Education and employment ==
George Kollias graduated from the Biology Department of the [[University of Athens]], Greece and performed doctoral studies in Molecular Biology from 1980 to 1984 at the [[National Hellenic Research Foundation]]. He continued with postdoctoral research in the field of gene structure and expression at the Laboratory of Gene Structure and Expression, [[National Institute for Medical Research]], Mill Hill, London, UK, and from 1990 to 2000 he established the Laboratory of [[Molecular genetics|Molecular Genetics]] at the [[Hellenic Pasteur Institute]] in Athens, Greece. From 2000 to 2002, he was appointed Director of the Institute for Immunology at the [[Alexander Fleming Biomedical Sciences Research Center|Biomedical Sciences Research Center "Alexander Fleming"]], and has served as the center's president and Scientific Director (2002–2010 & 2016–2020).<ref name=CV/> Since June 2014, he is Professor of Experimental Physiology at the Medical School of the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens.<ref>{{Cite web |title=George Kollias, Professor |url=https://physiology.med.uoa.gr/en/research-infrastructure-services/research-laboratories/george-kollias-professor/ |access-date=2026-01-15 |website=Εργαστήριο Φυσιολογίας "Φυσιολογείον" |language=en-US}}</ref> From 2020 to 2023 he served as Director of the [https://physiology.med.uoa.gr/en/ Department of Physiology].

== Research and innovation ==
In 1991, George Kollias' group was first to provide ''in vivo'', proof of principle studies, on deregulated [[Tumor necrosis factor|TNF]] production being causal to the development of chronic polyarthritis in a transgenic [[animal model]],<ref name="pmid1721867"/> and for showing originally that anti-huTNF antibody treatment was efficacious in treating the modeled disease (pg. 370<ref name="pmid26008591"/>). These studies were instrumental in mobilizing the interest of [[TNF inhibitor|anti-TNF industry]] and foreshadowed the success of the first clinical trials performed in RA in 1994. Further work in his lab provided insights into the function of TNF in host defense and the structure and function of secondary lymphoid organs, a work that more recently evolved into the establishment of TNFRI and [[NFkB]] signals specifically in [[follicular dendritic cells]] (FDCs) being of pivotal significance in the regulation of humoral [[B cell]] responses and [[Autoimmune disease|autoimmunity]]. Moreover, George Kollias' group demonstrated TNF's causal effect in the development of combined [[Crohn's disease]] and polyarthritis, and the contribution of transmembrane versus soluble TNF in the pathogenic processes. These studies offered a better understanding of the physiological function of TNF in health and disease and rationalized potential complications or optimizations of anti-TNF therapies in other diseases such as in [[Multiple sclerosis|MS]]. More recently, George Kollias introduced a novel pathogenic principle to explain the cellular basis of TNF function in gut/joint axis diseases, including spondyloarthropathies, by showing that [[Mesenchymal stem cell|mesenchymal cells]], namely synovial fibroblasts and intestinal subepithelial myofibroblasts, are common pathogenic targets of TNF sufficient to drive the chronic inflammatory and destructive disease process.<ref>[https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed?term=Kollias%20G%20AND%20(arthritis%20OR%20TNF) George Kollias' PubMed Publications]</ref> ] This pioneering research and findings offered the first in vivo evidence that fibroblasts activated by innate signals provide a dominant mechanism for the orchestration of complex pathologies such as chronic inflammation and fibrosis, and their deactivation may offer significant therapeutic potential. Animal models developed in his lab have been distributed to numerous academic and industrial laboratories around the world (over 200 Material Transfer Agreements in the last ten years). In 2005 he founded the first CRO-biotech spin-off of BSRC Fleming, [https://www.biomedcode.com Biomedcode Hellas SA] and in 2025 he founded [https://www.inolysis.com INOLYSIS], a company developing novel drug candidates against fibrosis.

== Distinctions ==
George Kollias is placed amongst the top cited European scientists in Rheumatology research for the period 1997 to 2008.<ref>[http://www.fleming.gr/files/Publication_Analysis_Rheumatology.pdf Rheumatology Publication Analysis 1997-2008]</ref> He has published over 230 primary research articles in peer-reviewed journals and more than 50 reviews and commentaries. His work has received over 49.000 citations and an h-index of 100 (data from Google Scholar<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=7RiVkaAAAAAJ&hl=el Google Scholar]</ref>). His laboratory is supported by several competitive grants from European Commission and National sources, as well as by the international [[biopharmaceutical]] industry.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.fleming.gr/en/investigators/Kollias/funding.html |title=International and national funding |access-date=11 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120325130242/http://www.fleming.gr/en/investigators/Kollias/funding.html |archive-date=25 March 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> From 2005 - 2009 Dr. Kollias coordinated a consortium of 24 EU organizations constituting the FP6 Network of Excellence MUGEN ("[[Functional genomics|Functional Genomics]] in mutant mouse models as tools to investigate the complexity of human immunological disease", 11M€).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mugen-noe.org/index.php?MODULE=bce%2Fapplication%2Fpages&Branch=N_N0000000001 |title=MUGEN NoE participants |access-date=26 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721174922/http://www.mugen-noe.org/index.php?MODULE=bce%2Fapplication%2Fpages&Branch=N_N0000000001 |archive-date=21 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was a core member of the Innovative Medicines Initiative (IMI) project BeTheCure (Total budget: 38 M€, 2011–2016)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://ki.se/ki/jsp/polopoly.jsp?l=en&d=130&a=118831&newsdep=130 |title=BeTheCure IMI Project |access-date=20 April 2011 |archive-date=14 April 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110414192925/http://ki.se/ki/jsp/polopoly.jsp?l=en&d=130&a=118831&newsdep=130 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He has been awarded two Advanced ERC grants: MCs-inTEST<ref>{{Cite web |title=New ERC Advanced Grant results: Over €660 million to 284 top researchers |date=2013-09-26 |url=http://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/press_release/files/press_release_adg2013_results.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140422172553/http://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/press_release/files/press_release_adg2013_results.pdf |archive-date=2014-04-22}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mesenchymal Cells of the Lamina Propria in Intestinal Epithelial and Immunological Homeostasis {{!}} MCs-inTEST {{!}} Project {{!}} Fact Sheet {{!}} FP7 |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/340217 |access-date=2026-01-15 |website=CORDIS {{!}} European Commission |language=en}}</ref>(ID: 340217, 2014–2019) highlighting the critical role of mesenchymal cells in intestinal epithelial and immunological homeostasis and BecomingCausal<ref>{{Cite web |title=Contextual specification of fibroblast-driven causalities in chronic intestinal inflammation and fibrosis {{!}} BecomingCausal {{!}} Project {{!}} Fact Sheet {{!}} HORIZON |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101055093 |access-date=2026-01-15 |website=CORDIS {{!}} European Commission |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=ERC Advanced grant awarded to George Kollias, Fleming Associated Researcher and Professor, Director of Physiology at the Medical School of Athens. |url=https://www.fleming.gr/impact/fleming-highlights/highlight-20220429}}</ref> (ID:101055093, 2022–2027) investigating the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying fibrosis in progressive IBD. In 2025 he was also awarded an ERC Proof of Concept grant to support the development of a novel oral therapy targeting fibroblast-driven inflammation and fibrosis in IBD via his startup company INOLYSIS.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A Fibroblast-Targeting Advanced Lead Mitigating Inflammation and Fibrosis in IBD {{!}} FIBROLEAD {{!}} Project {{!}} Fact Sheet {{!}} HORIZON |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101248226 |access-date=2026-01-15 |website=CORDIS {{!}} European Commission |language=en}}</ref>

George Kollias is an elected member of the European Molecular Biology Organization (EMBO)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.embo.org/embo-members/find-a-member.html |title=EMBO database |access-date=20 April 2011 |archive-date=22 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722091839/http://www.embo.org/embo-members/find-a-member.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> since 2000 and Member of the Biosciences Steering Group of the European Academies Science Advisory Panel (EASAC) since 2014. In recognition of eminent scientific discoveries and contributions to science, he was awarded the internationally acclaimed Carol-Nachman Award for Rheumatology<ref>[https://www.wiesbaden.de/leben-in-wiesbaden/stadtportrait/ehrenbuerger/content/carol-nachman-preis.php Carol Nachman Award]</ref> in 2014 and the first Galien Scientific Research Award, of Prix Galien Greece in 2015.<ref>[http://www.prixgalien.gr/galien-scientific-research-award/ Prix Galien Greece 2015]</ref> Dr. Kollias served as the National Representative of Greece for the ESFRI (2010–2012) and as member of the ESFRI strategic working group on Health and Food (2010 to date). George Kollias has been a member of the National Council on Research and Technology of the Ministry of Development (2001–2003 and 2005–2009) and has served as an elected President of the Council of the Directors of the Greek Research Centers (2009–2010). He serves as an advisor for scientific organizations and consults for industry. George Kollias also serves as invited speaker, chairman and member of the Organising and Scientific Committees of several scientific meetings throughout the world. George Kollias is Director of the Graduate Program in "[https://www.molecularbiomedicine.gr Molecular Biomedicine]" at the Medical School of the University of Athens (founded 2016).
